newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 20.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
CONGRESS, BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY SET TO SHRED GOVERNMENT

The minority coalition government will face embarrassing moments in the Budget session. Both the Congress and the Marxist Communist Party (CPM) were preparing to criticise it on economic and other issues. While the mood in the Congress was confrontationist, the main opposition party Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) would not spare any opportunity to come down heavily on the government. The BJP's ally, Samata Party, has already set the pace by giving a notice for no-confidence motion.
The Economic Times
FOODGRAIN PRICE INCREASE TO COMPROMISE SCHEME FOR POOR

Pressures within the ruling United Front coalition gave the food subsidy issue a bizarre aspect. A compromise formula being worked out sought to raise the issue price of foodgrain before providing it at half that price to people below the poverty line. The move was designed to keep both the Finance Minister and the Left parties happy by adopting a middle path. By raising the issue price before supplying it at half that price, the overall subsidy burden was sought to be contained.
SOROS, GE CAPS IN TALKS TO BUY ITC CLASSIC FINANCE

ITC was negotiating with GE Capital and Soros for selling off its financial arm, ITC Classic Finance. GE Capital recently acquired another major finance company, SRF Finance, for 480 million rupees. Soros was a serious contender as it was already in the process of acquiring ITC Classic's 22 percent stake in a group company, Classic Infrastructure Development, the infrastructure arm of ITC's financial services group. The remaining 78 percent equity was held by P. Chatterjee of Soros and GIC of Singapore.
TRADE DEFICIT MAY RISE TO $4 BLN

The Commerce Minister revised trade deficit estimates for the current fiscal from $2 billion to about $4 billion. The minister attributed the revision to the hardening oil prices in the international market. Accepting that negative growth in exports during November and December was a cause of concern, he, however, termed the export decline as temporary and said the year might end with export growth just below double digit figures.
FREE LICENCE MOVE IRKS SUGAR UNITS

The recent decision to introduce free licensing for new sugar units in place of an earlier plan of delicensing the industry raised eyebrows in the industry and trade circles. With a stock of eight million tonnes at the beginning of October 1996 when the current sugar season started, the free licensing was also ill-timed. The industry was expected to produce 15 million tonnes of sugar in the current crushing season. With domestic consumption estimated at around 13.5 million tonnes, the country may be saddled again with an unsold stock of 9.5 million tonnes.
VOLKSWAGEN MAY PICK PUNE FOR JOINT VENTURE

Volkswagen (VW) may choose Pune as the site for its 10 billion rupee car venture. The Maharashtra government has earmarked a 200-acre plot in an industrial area on the outskirts of Pune in anticipation. The project envisages production of 65,000 cars annually. The company planned to launch its Skoda model, which was currently made in the Czech Republic. VW's participation in the project would be through its wholly-owned German subsidiary, Audi. Both firms planned to hold 51 percent equity in the proposed project, for which they were looking for an Indian partner.
Financial Express
CHANGED COMPANIES ACT TO TAKE EFFECT FROM MARCH 1, 1997

The amended Companies Act was likely to be introduced from March 1, 1997. The changes granted voting rights to mutual funds, debarred firms which defaulted from raising fresh deposits/loans and gave a free hand to corporates to effect certain business decisions. The president had given his assent to the bill, which was passed by both the houses in December, 1996.
COMMITTEE SET UP TO EVOLVE NORMS FOR HIGHWAY PROJECTS

The government constituted an inter-secretarial committee to evolve standard build-operate-transfer terms for private sector participation in development of national highways. The body would evolve a concession agreement with a view to address the concerns of prospective investors and achieve economy, efficiency and transparency.
RAJASTHAN EMBRACES SOLAR POWER

Rajasthan proposed a total generation of 300 megawatts by tapping solar energy, the first massive generation of power ever attempted in the world by taking the solar route. Letters of intent have gone to Energen International of Sri Lanka, Amoco-Enron Solar Power Development of the United States and Sun Source (India). The state electricity board (RSEB) had signed power purchase agreements (PPA) with Amoco-Enron and Sun Source, assuring a total generation of 100 megawatts.
Business Standard
CORPORATE TAX RATE TO BE CUT, SURCHARGE TO GO

The government was set to withdraw the surcharge on corporate income tax in the budget to be presented on February 28, officials said. They added it was possible that the corporate tax rate would also be cut from 40 to 35 percent. Domestic companies at present were liable to pay income tax at the rate of 40 percent. Those with an annual income of 75,000 rupees were also liable to pay a surcharge of 7.5 percent on the income tax payable by them.
HOTELS MAY LEAD GOVERMENT'S SELLOFF PLAN

The Industry Minister indicated the government would be willing to kick off its disinvestment programme with hotels followed by the tourism industry. These sectors, seen as non- core, non-strategic areas, were expected to face least resistance, sources said. It was felt that divestment of majority stake, including divestment of management control, would be acceptable to all constituents of the ruling coalition, the trade unions and the opposition.
FUJITSU IN PARLEYS WITH ESSAR COMMUNICATION

Fujitsu was negotiating with Essar Commission, the basic telecom services letter of intent holder for Punjab, for an equipment supply contract and an equity stake in the firm. Fujitsu India sources confirmed the negotiations while Essar executives said they were talking to a number of equipment suppliers and Fujitsu was only one of them. The size of the deal was expected to be in the region of some 6-7 billion rupees. This would include supply of exchanges, fibre-optic cables, microwave radio, associated equipment and the local access loop.
The Observer
NOD FOR DRAFT FARM POLICY

State agriculture ministers approved the revised draft agriculture policy resolution which aimed to achieve 4.5 percent growth rate by promoting higher capital formation and scientific farming. The Agriculture Minister said another meeting of state ministers would be held to concretise action plans for achieving the proposed growth for each state. A note was also taken of the fact that many of the Eighth Plan targets for agriculture had been missed.
OIL AND NATURAL GAS CORPORATION RIG CATCHES FIRE

A massive blowout occurred at one of the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) rigs engaged in oil drilling operations when it caught fire in East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh. ONGC officials said the fire resulted in 100 metre high flames, filling the skyline with thick black clouds.
Business Line
INDIA REJECTS BASIC TELEPHONY TO SATELLITE SERVICES

India refused to allow any of the satellite services to operate basic telephony services in the country. This barred the country from joining any of the satellite consortia or from availing itself of their services already accessible in India. The tough stand on the future of basic telephony was evident when Indian negotiators at the World Trade Organisation negotiations on basic services decided to deny market access to any of the satellite consortia.
